page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4r.16xlarge is an x86_64 virtualization instance belonging to the Local SSDs instance family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system provides 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 3839 GB of integrated local solid-state drive storage.

Network infrastructure on this instance provides a baseline bandwidth capacity of 32 Gbps, while graphics processing units are absent. Because this instance combines high memory density with substantial local solid-state disk capacity, it achieves balanced qualitative cost efficiency for resource-heavy applications by eliminating external disk latency and network storage transaction overheads. Tradeoffs include the ephemeral nature of direct-attached local storage, which requires data replication strategies across instances to safeguard against host failures.

The hardware configuration is tailored for memory-intensive and I/O-sensitive enterprise operations. Primary workload fits include in-memory databases, large-scale search engines, distributed caching layers such as Redis, analytical data processing, real-time logging clusters, and low-latency transactional database management systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4r.16xlarge is a memory-dense, storage-focused instance type within the Local SSDs family, deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. It integrates 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio, and bundles 3839 GB of local SSD storage alongside a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include GPU acceleration hardware. Its architectural profile is engineered for high throughput and reduced I/O latency, offering strong operational efficiency for deployments requiring massive memory tables alongside fast direct disk access. This makes it appropriate for distributed NoSQL databases, memory-cached transactional systems, large-scale relational database engines, and real-time big data processing workloads.
